newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to shut down 18 nuclear reactors by 2010.
newsitem.headline: Russia to shut down 18 nuclear reactors by 2010.

text.p: Russia, responding to concern about the safety of its first generation nuclear reactors, plans to shut down a further 18 units by the year 2010, a nuclear energy ministry official told Reuters on Friday.
Vladislav Petrov said four reactors had already been mothballed and 18 more would be closed. New stations were planned to replace them over the next six to 10 years.

Nuclear power accounts for around 12 percent of the electricity generated in Russia. Most new projects have been delayed since the 1986 Chernobyl disaster, but some of the planned stations are now being built.
"Four more stable reactors, 1,000 megawatts each, are under construction at power stations in Kalinin, Kursk, Rostov and Sosnovy Bor (near St Petersburg)," said Petrov.
"Of course, the government plans the construction of many more reactors but everything depends on sufficient financing."
"There are 29 nuclear reactors operating in Russia, nine of which are first generation but deeply modernised and functioning well" Petrov said.
